lines.text: Do you know how a paper shredder works? It's not one blade chopping paper. It's two rows of spinning steel discs.
Inside, two shafts of sharp discs turn towards each other. They grab the paper and pull it through, like a mangle with teeth.
Simple shredders cut long strips. Fast, but strips can be put back together.
In 1979, after the US embassy in Tehran was taken over, students spent years gluing shredded strips back into readable documents.
So better shredders cut both ways. Cross cut and micro cut machines turn a page into confetti, thousands of tiny pieces.
There's even a standard for it, from P one to P seven. At the top level, each piece is smaller than a grain of rice.
Orbi gives files a shredder too. By default, 30 minutes after you send, the locked pieces on the server are deleted. You can pick anything from five to 30 minutes.
